lines.english: "Yes, they should be arriving at the gate soon."
"Don't use any name boards, okay? The mass media might find out. Do your best to recognize them yourself."
"Leave it to me! I remember their faces perfectly!"
"Though they've probably forgotten what you look like, Miyo-chan."
"Oh, don't dampen my spirits like that, President."
"Well, in any case, there's likely going to be crowds since it's Christmas, so do make sure to not lose sight of them."
"Yes, it certainly does seem more crowded than usual. But it's all concentrated around the departure gates. Families, couples… friends…"
"Yes… I'm sorry for bringing up the topic when it has nothing to do with you, Miyo-chan.
"Whose fault do you think it is that my life turned out this way!?"
"If anything, you should be grateful to your employer for providing you with such a convenient excuse."
"…Oh, hey! I found them! Excuse me for a moment."
"Kazusa-saaan! Kitahara-saaan! Over here!"
"Cut it out already, Kazusa… Why do you have to insist on being so pointlessly stubborn?"
"You're the one who should cut it out! I've already told you I'll forgive you if you simply apologize. Why can't you do something as simple as that!?"
"I'll tell you precisely why I can't apologize… That's because this time, I haven't done a single thing wrong."
"U-Umm… Kazusa-san…"
"That's it, I'm divorcing you! It's a Narita divorce for us!"
"Don't misuse your terms. A Narita divorce is synonymous with an instant divorce. We've been married for years now so it doesn't apply to us."
"I'll say it again, I despise how you have to find fault with everything I say, and grasp at every straw!"
"Oh, that's an absolute honor! I didn't become who I am because I wanted you to like me."
"Don't talk! Don't speak! Don't open your mouth! I never want to hear your voice again!"
"Those all mean the same thing. We're back in Japan now, so you should use proper Japanese."
"Aaah, shut up, shut up!"
"…President."
"Were you able to find them?"
"Forget about me… I don't think those two can find each other… Um, on a mental level."
"Oh, goodness me."
"Now then, I'll be sleeping in this room… Don't you dare come in."
"I could say the same. Apologize and cry all you want about how lonely you are later, I still won't let you into my bed!"
"Like hell I'd ever do that! Not ever in my life!"
"See you then! Good night!"
"Shut up!"
"…Haah."
After uttering her parting remark for the umpteenth time, Kazusa vigorously shut the door and disappeared into the other room.
…I'm seriously glad I picked a suite. It would be beyond awkward if we had to stay in the same room together all night.
"Ah, um… um, um, um!"
"…I'm sorry, Kudou-san. I know this was the absolute worst timing for all of this."
And I'm beyond sorry for all of this.
This person, or more specifically Kudou Miyoko of the Japanese branch of Touma Youko Office, showed us to our suite despite looking completely taken aback,
"Anyway, you should rest for today. I'll come pick you two up tomorrow morning."
"I'm really sorry. Pass my apologies to Youko-san as well."
"Ah, it's okay, the president doesn't seem to mind at all… She couldn't stop laughing on the other end of the line, in fact."
"Ha, hahaha… hah…"
Well, I can deduce two things from Kudou-san's remark.
The first being that Youko-san is still doing alright.
And the second being that Kudou-san is really worried about our quarrel…
"Anyway, good night."
"You too, good nig…"
"It's surely just a pointless worry of mine, but you two don't intend on being like this for your entire stay in Japan, right!? You'll make up, right!?"
"Ha, hahaha, haaah…"
Walking away, Kudou-san kept glaring at me with a grim expression until it was no longer visible behind the closing door.
Well, it's not like I don't understand where she's coming from, and I do feel bad for her, but this matter is one I refuse to back down on.
I may be Kazusa's man and faithful employee, but that doesn't mean I have to tolerate her selfish childishness every single time.
But still… thinking back, this trip to Japan was nothing but trouble from the start.
I mean, yeah, it was my fault at first.
My business meeting back home was prolonged, causing us to miss our flight, and causing Kazusa to have to wait at the airport for five hours.
But she didn't seem to mind at the time. The problems only started after we boarded the next flight, and the transit that followed.
A certain someone began to whine that she couldn't sleep and wanted pudding on the plane. (Guess who!)
Inside a store at the transit airport, a certain someone made a scene over losing her wallet. (Guess who!)
After waking up, a certain someone watched a romance movie, but flipped out when the main characters broke up at the end despite being in love. (Guess who!)
…See what I'm talking about? I was only at fault in the beginning, but the rest is all on her.
As I murmur these complaints to myself, I turn on the shower and let the warm water pour down on me.
"…Haah."
I can feel my stiff muscles finally start to relax after hours of doing nothing but sitting.
"…I'm sorry."
In the same vein, my stubborn heart also starts to relax a little.
Yes, the one who started it is to blame for everything. I'm the one who put her in that mood to begin with.
This was Kazusa's long-awaited return to Japan.
…After years of running away, we've finally returned to the place we once called home.
It's unreasonable to expect her to remain calm on such a special occasion.
And besides, the problem isn't just the fact that we've come back.
There's something waiting for us here; something that makes it even harder for the two of us to remain calm.
"…Yes."
That's right, I should go and apologize.
When I leave the shower, I should calm myself down a little, call her, knock on her door, and bow my head…
"Uwaaaaaah, Haruki! I'm so lonely!"
"Uwaaaah!?"
But before I could even reflect on my actions…
"You, you… How can you stand there and take a shower so nonchalantly!? Doesn't abandoning me affect you in the slightest!?"
"I haven't abandoned you long enough to have abandoned you yet!"
"No, don't say that… It was all my fault! I'll apologize! I'll do anything! So please don't abandon me like that!"
"Try to stay angry for at least an hour. Give me time to reflect on my actions…"
"No… Let me apologize. I'm sorry, I'm sorry, Haruki."
Kazusa clings to my body while I'm still completely naked and dripping wet.
And from the still running showerhead above, warm water pours down on the both of us.
"You'll get wet."
"That's fine."
"If you stay cold like this, you'll end up catching one yourself, you know."
"It's okay. You'll keep me warm, Haruki."
"Kazusa…"
"…Right?"
Such a stupid reason to get soaked, yet Kazusa looks so beautiful, cute, and utterly helpless all the same…
"Yeah…"
"Nhm, mh… H-Haru…!"
In this cramped hotel bathroom, surrounded by hot water, we bring each other into a passionate and powerful embrace.
"Kitahara-saan, Kazusa-saan, it's about time you woke up."
"Mh…"
"Ah, good morning!"
"Hm? Ah, good morning… I'm sorry, what time is it?"
"Ehm, if I may, it's almost twelve…"
"Huh, is it so late already? I'm so sorry, I'll get ready immedi… Uaaah!?"
"…Kitahara-san?"
"S-Sorry, it's nothing… Hey, wake up already! You can't stay half asleep forever!"
"Don't worry, I've been awake for a while now…"
"But your actions make you seem half asleep! Hey, cut that out! Not so hard… Ngh!"
"Hey… Let's do it again."
"Kudou-san is already outside the room!"
"Miyo-chan wouldn't mind waiting a little more."
"No, we can't do that… In fact, if we linger any longer, she'll definitely find out what we're up to."
"So what? We've finally reconciled now… And besides, you were completely engrossed in it until sunrise yourself, Haruki."
"Only because you kept pestering me to… Ah, no, Kazusa, I told you… stop that…!"
"Nope, I won't stop. Mh, mhm… Haruki, mmh… aaah…"
"…Maybe I should quit this job."
